h1: The 5 Best Desktop Printer Stands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Desktop Printer Stands 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five desktop printer stands and risers compared on storage, cable control, mobility and fit for compact printers.
summary: The HUANUO printer stand is our top pick because it is purpose-built, with a drawer, cable cutouts and locking casters. The HOOBRO two-tier stand adds a charging station for small offices. The WALI riser is the cheapest simple lift, and the Liitrton and Hovadova stands are low rolling platforms that suit light printers.
intro: The most common mistake with a printer stand is buying on looks and ignoring depth and weight. A stand that is half an inch too shallow lets the printer's tray hang over the edge, and a stand rated for a light inkjet will sag under a laser all-in-one. Measure your printer's footprint first.

We ranked five options on paper using the spec sheets and owner reports. Dedicated stands rank above repurposed risers and CPU platforms, and storage, cable control and mobility decide the order within each group. Prices appear as buckets.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: The only one here built from the start to hold a printer.
products.description:
This stand tops out at a 14.1-inch maximum shelf height and adds a storage drawer, cable cutouts and locking caster wheels. It falls in the $25-50 bracket.

It leads the field because the drawer swallows paper and cartridges while the cutouts keep the power cord out of sight. The HOOBRO below is smaller and lacks the rolling base.

Pick it if the printer shares a desk with a lot of supplies. The caveat is that its height limit means very tall printers may not fit under a shelf above.
products.idealFor: Desks needing paper and ink storage.
products.skipIf: You only need a few inches of lift.

products.name: HOOBRO 2-Tier Printer Stand with Charging Station
products.verdict: A compact two-tier unit with a charging station built in.
products.description:
HOOBRO's two-tier stand includes a built-in charging station, a rustic brown and black finish, and is sized for small home offices. It can sit on a desk or beneath it. Expect $25-50.

The charging station is the hook: you power the printer and a phone from one place. It ranks second since it offers no drawer or casters.

It suits a tidy small office where the second tier holds paper. Check the printer depth against the shelf before ordering.
products.idealFor: A small office needing printer plus charging.

products.name: WALI Computer Monitor Stand for Desk, Adjustable Laptop Riser
products.verdict: A cheap lift with some space underneath, but not made for printers.
products.description:
This riser has adjustable height, an underneath storage area and a compact flat platform. It is marketed for monitors and laptops, and costs under $25, the lowest in the ranking.

It ranks third because it works for a light printer and frees desk space, yet offers no cable management or weight rating aimed at printers.

Fine for a small inkjet. Do not trust it with a heavy laser all-in-one.

products.name: Hovadova Adjustable Mobile CPU Stand (Black)
products.verdict: A ventilated rolling base that doubles as a printer riser.
products.description:
Built as a CPU tower stand, this one has a ventilated platform, four casters and adjustable width in black. It costs under $25.

The ventilation helps a printer breathe, and the casters let you slide it out to clear a jam. It ranks fourth because it is a low platform with no storage and wasn't made for printers.

Pick it for under-desk placement of a compact printer. A white version exists if you prefer that color.
products.skipIf: You want a shelf or drawer.

products.name: Liitrton Mobile CPU Stand Adjustable Computer Tower Stand
products.verdict: A plain rolling base for the tightest budgets.
products.description:
Another CPU tower stand, the Liitrton offers adjustable width, rolling casters and a low, flat platform with a compact footprint. It costs under $25.

It sits last because it lacks the ventilation of the Hovadova and offers no storage or cable help.

Choose it as a cheap wheeled base. The platform is low, so it will not lift a printer to eye level.
products.idealFor: Moving a compact printer under a desk.

whatMatters.detail: A laser all-in-one can weigh far more than an inkjet, and a stand that sags gets unsafe. Check the listing for a stated load rating and compare to your printer's weight in its manual.
Printers have output trays that extend beyond the body. If the shelf is too shallow the tray hangs off. Measure your printer's depth and compare to the shelf dimension.
Printers need both power and a data cable. Cutouts or grommets keep cords from tangling. Look for the words cable management in the title.
Wheels make clearing jams and cleaning easier, but unlocked wheels can drift. Look for locking casters in the specs.
Printers produce heat while running. A ventilated platform improves airflow underneath. Check for open or slotted designs.

faq.q: Can a CPU stand hold a printer?
faq.a: A light one, yes. Check the weight limit first, since CPU stands are rated for towers, not printers.

faq.q: How much shelf depth do I need?
faq.a: Measure the printer plus its output tray and add a little margin.
They keep the stand still when the printer is working. The HUANUO lists locking casters.

faq.q: Is the HOOBRO worth the charging station?
faq.a: If you charge a phone at your desk, yes. Otherwise the HUANUO offers more storage.

faq.q: Can I put a printer under a desk?
faq.a: Yes, but leave room to open the lid and clear jams. The Hovadova and HOOBRO suit this.
Carts add height but need floor space. For desk use a compact stand fits better.

finalTake: The HUANUO Printer Stand is the right default because it is made for printers and organizes the supplies around them. Take the HOOBRO for a tight office with charging, and the WALI riser if you only want a quick lift.
